deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no derivations, formulas, computations or figures. It is a page of German prose notes, apparently from a history lecture or a copied textbook, on ancient history, specifically the campaign of Alexander the Great.

The text runs on from the previous page, which ended mid-sentence at the Battle of Issus (333 BC). It says:
- Alexander chose ground in a plain surrounded by mountains and protected or crossed by a river. Historically this is the Pinarus.
- He won the battle. On the Persian side were 30,000 Greek mercenaries ('griechische Hülfstruppen'), and these were also defeated.
- Margin: Darius had to flee, but Alexander captured the royal family.
- Darius made an offer (historically a peace offer) of half his empire. Alexander refused it, and he treated Darius's family magnanimously. The words 'behandelte er' are an interlinear addition in a different (bluish) ink.
- Alexander then entered Phoenicia and subdued all of it except Tyre.
- He decided to besiege Tyre, which had two important consequences: (1) as master of Tyre he became master of the sea; (2) it opened his way to Egypt.

The next page (129) continues with the mole, the seven-month siege (332 BC) and the founding of Alexandria.

The neat, rounded hand and the plain schoolroom content suggest student lecture notes bound into the bundle. This is probably not Gauss's own working, though authorship cannot be decided from this page alone. Nothing here needs mathematical reconstruction.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible, since there is no mathematics. Historical content: the 30,000 Greek mercenaries at Issus matches the ancient sources (Arrian). Darius's offer of the land west of the Euphrates (roughly 'half the empire') is historically placed after the siege of Tyre, not directly after Issus. This is a common compression in textbooks.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'durchwatete sich der Fluß hinterm[?] Schlacht[?]' is doubtful. Context (Issus) suggests the river named is the Pinarus, so read something like '... sich durch den Fluß Pinarus ...'. The ending of the line is uncertain in the image.
'Freundesantrag' should most likely read 'Friedensantrag' (peace offer). The image reads roughly 'Friedensantrag', and this fits the history.
Margin: punctuate as 'Darius mußte d. Flucht ergreifen, hingegen die königliche Familie bekam Alexander in d. Hände.'
'behandelte er' is an interlinear insertion in a different (bluish) ink above 'Seine Familie'. The transcription marks the insertion but not the change of ink.
